items.question: What is my educational background?
items.answer:
Rudra holds a Master of Computer Science from the University of Wollongong, completed between July 2023 and September 2025, and a B.Tech in Computer Science & Engineering with a Data Science Specialisation from Gujarat State Fertilizers and Chemicals University, completed between 2019 and 2023 [[cite:3]].

During the Master's degree, coursework concentrated on machine learning, big data, computer vision and security, aligning with a Machine Learning and Big Data major, and included subjects such as Computer Vision Algorithms and Systems, Machine Learning Algorithms and Applications, Big Data Analytics, Data Management Systems, and Web Development [[cite:8]][[cite:6]]. Rudra graduated with High Distinctions in Programming and Data Structures, Web Development, Strategic Network Design, and the Professional Capstone Project, and earned Distinctions in Big Data Analytics, Security Essentials, AI and Cybersecurity, and System Analysis and Project Management [[cite:6]]. The Professional Capstone Project was the largest subject at 12 credit points and finished with a High Distinction [[cite:6]].

The undergraduate degree covered foundational and mathematics subjects, core computer science topics like programming, data structures and algorithms, operating systems, computer networks and web technologies, as well as electronics and hardware subjects such as digital electronics and microprocessor interfacing, alongside professional subjects and industrial internships across multiple semesters [[cite:5]].

items.question: Which AI/ML frameworks have I used?
items.answer:
Rudra has used a range of AI/ML frameworks and tools including scikit-learn, PyTorch, LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Sentence-Transformers, along with rank-bm25 for hybrid retrieval [[cite:1]]. He has also worked with vector databases such as ChromaDB, and applied techniques like embeddings, prompt engineering, multi-agent orchestration, and hallucination guardrails [[cite:1]]. Additionally, his broader skill set includes Hugging Face Transformers, Hugging Face Inference API, TensorFlow, and ReAct-based agent systems [[cite:2]].

He has integrated multiple LLM providers into his work, including Groq (Llama-3.3-70B), Together AI, Anthropic Claude, and the OpenAI API [[cite:1]]. His projects, such as PersonaQuery and HealthEcho, reflect hands-on use of these frameworks for building RAG pipelines, inference APIs, and evaluation harnesses [[cite:4,5]].

items.question: What internships have I done?
items.answer:
Rudra completed several internships during his studies. At Tntra Engineering in Vadodara, he first worked as a Full Stack Intern from June to July 2022, building industry-level web applications and learning the process flow of projects in a service-provider organisation [[cite:1]]. This was followed by a Multi Domain Intern role at Tntra from September to December 2022, a rotational training program covering data science, IoT, Industry 4.0, cyber security, and cloud computing, where he worked in a three-person team under senior developer guidance [[cite:2]]. The resume consolidates both Tntra stints into a single listing as "Engineering Intern (Full Stack + Multi-Domain)" spanning June to December 2022, describing shipped web app modules and multi-domain training in web development, cloud, and security [[cite:3]].

Additionally, Rudra completed an Android Application Development Internship at TSPL from January to July 2023 in Vadodara, India, where he built an Android app end-to-end with backend REST APIs and analytics charts using Java/Spring Boot and MySQL [[cite:3]].

items.question: Summarize my professional profile.
items.answer:
Rudra's professional background centers on machine learning, big data, and AI-focused coursework, including strong performance in programming, data structures, web development, and security-related subjects [[cite:2]]. His capstone project, the largest single subject in his studies, was completed with a High Distinction, reflecting sustained academic strength in his major [[cite:2]].

His practical work includes building PersonaQuery, a retrieval-augmented generation assistant that answers questions about him using his own documents with inline citations and safeguards against prompt injection [[cite:6]]. The system uses a hand-built hybrid retrieval pipeline combining dense embeddings and BM25 keyword search fused via Reciprocal Rank Fusion, along with section-aware chunking and a custom vector store, rather than frameworks like LangChain or LlamaIndex as sometimes described elsewhere [[cite:6]][[cite:5]]. This reflects a pattern of hands-on, self-implemented technical work rather than relying solely on external libraries [[cite:5]][[cite:3]].

He has also engaged in professional development through structured programs, such as completing a job simulation focused on prompt and contextual engineering skills for automating professional workflows [[cite:8]].

Inference: Based on his coursework emphasis on machine learning, big data, and security, combined with his hands-on engineering of a custom RAG pipeline (embeddings, BM25, RRF fusion) rather than off-the-shelf frameworks, Rudra appears well-suited for roles in applied machine learning engineering or AI systems development that require both academic grounding and practical, from-scratch implementation skills [[cite:2]][[cite:6]].

items.question: What is the title of the patent?
items.answer: The patent is titled "Intelligent Face Recognition System Using Deep Recurrent Neural Network" [[cite:1,3]]. It was filed under Application No. 202211058943 A in India, with the application published in the Patent Office Journal No. 42/2022 [[cite:1,5]].

items.question: What is the patent application number?
items.answer: The patent application number is 202211058943 A, filed on 15 October 2022 for the Intelligent Face Recognition System Using Deep Recurrent Neural Network [[cite:2,3,4]].

items.question: What neural network architectures does the patent describe?
items.answer: The patent describes a face recognition system that combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a recurrent neural network (RNN) [[cite:5]]. The CNN and RNN together form a key generation module that outputs a consistent key value using sample facial images of a person [[cite:5]]. This architecture is also reflected in the patent's title, which explicitly names the invention as an intelligent face recognition system using a deep recurrent neural network [[cite:1,3]].

items.question: What is the patent journal number?
items.answer: The patent was published in Patent Office Journal No. 42/2022, dated 21 October 2022 [[cite:1,3]].

items.question: What is the Cognitive-Chair project about?
items.answer:
The Cognitive-Chair is an AI-based brain-sensing wheelchair designed to assist paraplegic and quadriplegic individuals [[cite:5]]. It uses a Brain Sensing Headband employing Electro-oculography to capture neural data, which is transferred to a mobile application and then relayed to the wheelchair so it can operate according to the user's neuro signals rather than physical input [[cite:4,5]]. The research was carried out during a B.Tech degree at GSFC University and involved co-authors including Kshitij Joshi, Abhilasha Vyas, and Smit Joshi, with Rudra Joshi as a co-author [[cite:1,5]].

The project earned significant recognition, winning the Best Paper Award at the 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Speech Technology (AIST-2022), organized by the Centre of Excellence - Artificial Intelligence [[cite:5,8]]. It was also published on IEEE Xplore [[cite:5,8]]. The work additionally led to the filing of an Indian government patent application for an Intelligent Face Recognition System using Deep Recurrent Neural Network [[cite:1,5,6]].

items.question: What are the main brainwave frequencies mentioned?
items.answer: The main brainwave frequencies mentioned are Gamma, Beta, Alpha, Theta, and Delta [[cite:1,2]]. Gamma waves are associated with the acquisition of new information in the brain [[cite:1]]. Beta waves relate to focused conscious thinking during cognitive and real-world tasks [[cite:1,2]]. Alpha waves are linked to calm, relaxed thinking and represent the brain's default resting state [[cite:1]]. Theta waves are most common during sleep and deep meditation [[cite:1]]. Delta waves are characterized by low frequency and are associated with deep tranquility, relaxation, and dream formation during the deepest states of sleep or meditation [[cite:1]].

items.question: What microcontroller is used in the wheelchair design?
items.answer: The wheelchair design uses an Arduino microcontroller to process data received from the Android application and control the wheelchair motors and other hardware [[cite:1]]. This microcontroller is linked to the mobile application that runs the control algorithm, enabling it to manage the wheelchair's movement based on EEG/EOG signals [[cite:2]].

items.question: Which bluetooth module does the system use?
items.answer: The system uses the HC-06 bluetooth module for wireless transmission of signals between the headband/microcontroller setup [[cite:2]]. This module functions to manage the wireless communication channel clearly and without delay, connecting to smartphones for data transmission [[cite:1]].

items.question: What is a Brain-Computer Interface according to the paper?
items.answer:
A Brain-Computer Interface (BCI), also called a Brain-Machine Interface or Direct Neural Interface, is a technology that allows users to communicate with machines or external devices using brain signals instead of the normal output pathways of peripheral nerves and muscles, giving humans the ability to control machines directly [[cite:1]]. It is described as one of the most promising and increasingly popular technologies for assisting and enhancing communication and control for people with motor paralysis, such as those with paraplegia, quadriplegia, stroke, spinal cord injury, cerebral palsy, or ALS [[cite:2,7]].

A BCI system is composed of three main parts: electrodes that record electric, magnetic, or metabolic brain activity, a processing pipeline that interprets these signals and extracts relevant features to generate commands, and a computer or external device that acts on those generated commands [[cite:5]]. BCIs can be categorized as invasive, non-invasive, or semi-invasive, depending on how the sensors interact with the brain, ranging from microelectrodes inserted directly into brain tissue to sensors placed on the scalp to detect electrical potentials such as EEG or magnetic fields such as MEG [[cite:5]].
